I could really use my network for help or advice. Let me preface this by saying I love my daughter and there is nothing I would not do for her. My teenage daughter recently crossed 100,000 subscribers on YouTube. She has worked extremely hard for the last couple of years. Her content is wholesome, creative, and artistic, and she has mentored many younger people in her community. As her father, I could not be prouder. Due to a technicality involving a linked account from years ago, YouTube is currently not issuing her the Silver Creator Award (Play Button). She has gone through the normal support channels without success. Support indicated that exceptions can be granted in certain cases. I’ve reached out privately to a couple of people at YouTube , but I’m also posting here in case anyone has insight, has dealt with a similar eligibility flag, or knows someone on the Creator Awards / Partner Support side who might be able to take a second look. I’m not looking for PR and I’m not publicly naming her channel (she is underage and would be mortified if this circulated widely). Just hoping for advice or a useful connection. For every reaction this post receives, I’ll donate $1 to Beast Philanthropy (up to $5,001). Thank you for reading. Kai

Y Combinator just updated their Request for Startups 🔥 Here are 13 ideas they ACTUALLY want to fund in the Fall 2026 batch: Getting into YC with Fluently (AI English tutor, GetFluently.app ) was the single biggest shortcut of my founder life. If you're applying to the fall batch, this list is your unfair advantage 👇 1. The Primer (an AI tutor that raises a kid's reading level) 2. The Future of American Defense 3. A Cloud for Small Software 4. Multiplayer AI 5. Compute at Sea 6. AI-Powered Consumer Products for 1 Billion People 7. AI for the Aging Population 8. New Operating Systems for the Physical World 9. The Best Time to Build in Crypto 10. Data for the Real World 11. Proving You're Human 12. AI-Native Compliance Infrastructure 13. Self-Maintaining APIs Here’re the 3 patterns that stand out: First, AI is moving into the physical world. Education, healthcare, defense, finance, infrastructure, and work itself, all of it rebuilt around models that touch something real. Second, the software requests are about problems agents created. Small software needs somewhere to live. Agent sessions need more than 1 person in the room. APIs break codebases and now an agent can open the fix. Third, look at who wrote it. YC partners, founders in the current batch, and the sitting US Secretary of the Army. People who hit these problems this year and wrote down what they needed. -- You don't need to build one of these to get in. But if one of them is already the problem you think about daily, take it as a signal.

We’re also seeing great adoption of Gemini Enterprise, used by 90% of the Fortune 100, as well as strong demand for our security solutions.
